مِنْ أَوْلِيَائِكَ وَ أَلْحِقْنِي بِهِمْ وَ اِجْعَلْنِي مُسَلِّماً لِمَنْ قَالَ بِالصِّدْقِ عَلَيْكَ مِنْهُمْ اَللَّهُمَّ وَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ تُحِيطَ بِي خَطِيئَتِي وَ ظُلْمِي وَ إِسْرَافِي عَلَى نَفْسِي وَ اِتِّبَاعِي لِهَوَايَ وَ اِشْتِغَالِي بِشَهَوَاتِي فَيَحُولَ ذَلِكَ بَيْنِي وَ بَيْنَ رَحْمَتِكَ وَرِضْوَانِكَ فَأَكُونَ مَنْسِيّاً عِنْدَكَ مُتَعَرِّضاً لِسَخَطِكَ وَنَقِمَتِكَ اَللَّهُمَّ وَفِّقْنِي لِكُلِّ عَمَلٍ صَالِحٍ تَرْضَى بِهِ عَنِّي وَ قَرِّبْنِي إِلَيْكَ زُلْفَى اَللَّهُمَّ كَمَا كَفَيْتَ نَبِيَّكَ مُحَمَّداً صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ هَوْلَ عَدُوِّهِ وَ فَرَّجْتَ هَمَّهُ وَ كَشَفْتَ غَمَّهُ وَصَدَقْتَهُ وَعْدَكَ وَأَنْجَزْتَ لَهُ عَهْدَكَ اَللَّهُمَّ فَبِذَلِكَ فَاكْفِنِي هَوْلَ هَذِهِ اَلسَّنَةِ وَآفَاتِهَا وَأَسْقَامَهَا وَفِتْنَتَهَا وَشُرُورَهَا وَأَحْزَانَهَا وَ ضِيقَ اَلْمَعَاشِ فِيهَا وَبَلِّغْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ كَمَالَ اَلْعَافِيَةِ بِتَمَامِ دَوَامِ اَلنِّعْمَةِ عِنْدِي إِلَى مُنْتَهَى أَجَلِي أَسْأَلُكَ سُؤَالَ مَنْ أَسَاءَ وَ ظَلَمَ وَ اِعْتَرَفَ وَ أَسْأَلُكَ أَنْ تَغْفِرَ لِي مَا مَضَى مِنَ اَلذُّنُوبِ اَلَّتِي حَصَرَتْهَا حَفَظَتُكَ وَ أَحْصَتْهَا كِرَامُ مَلاَئِكَتِكَ عَلَيَّ وَ أَنْ تَعْصِمَنِي إِلَهِي مِنَ اَلذُّنُوبِ فِيمَا بَقِيَ مِنْ عُمُرِي إِلَى مُنْتَهَى أَجَلِي يَا اَللَّهُ يَا رَحْمَانُ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَهْلِ بَيْتِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آتِنِي كُلَّمَا سَأَلْتُكَ وَ رَغِبْتُ إِلَيْكَ فِيهِ فَإِنَّكَ أَمَرْتَنِي بِالدُّعَاءِ وَ تَكَفَّلْتَ بِالْإِجَابَةِ يَا أَرْحَمَ اَلرَّاحِمِينَ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Qummi, from Sa’adan ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said in the farewell of the Month of Ramadan: “O’ Allah (swt), indeed You (azj) have said in Your revealed Book, upon the tongue of Your sent Prophet (saws), Your blessings be upon him and his family, and Your word is truth: ‘The Month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur’an’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185); and now this Month of Ramadan has passed by. So I ask You (azj) by Your Noble Face and by Your complete words; if there remains upon me any sin which You (azj) have not yet forgiven me for, or that You (azj) will punish me for, or take me to account for (I ask You (azj)) that the dawn of this night not rise, nor this month come to a close, except that You (azj) have forgiven it for me, O’ Most Merciful of the merciful. O’ Allah (swt), to You (azj) belongs all praise with all forms of praise, its first and its last, what You (azj) have praised Yourself with, and what the praising creatures have said for You (azj) those who strive, enumerate, and devote themselves in Your remembrance and gratitude; those whom You (azj) have assisted in fulfilling Your due, right from among the various ranks of Your creation of the angels brought near, and the prophets and the messengers, and the various ranks of those who speak and glorify You (azj) from among all the worlds. For the fact that You (azj) caused us to reach the Month of Ramadan, And (that) upon us was from Your blessings, And in our possession from Your allotment, And Your beneficence, And the manifestation of Your generosity for that, to You (azj) belongs the utmost praise; everlasting, enduring, settled, perpetual praise that never comes to an end, throughout all eternity. Exalted is Your praise. You (azj) assisted us in it until You (azj) enabled us, to fulfill its fasting and its nightly standing in prayer and devotion. And whatever acts of righteousness, or gratitude, or remembrance that we performed in it, O’ Allah (swt), accept it from us with the best of Your acceptance, And through Your overlooking, Your pardon, Your forgiveness, Your clemency, and the reality of Your pleasure until You (azj) grant us therein every desired good, and abundant granted gifts, and grant us safety from every feared matter and acquired sin. O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by the greatest of what any of Your creation has ever asked You (azj), by the nobility of Your Names, the abundance of Your praise, and the specificity of Your invocation, to send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), And to make this month of ours the greatest Month of Ramadan to pass over us since You (azj) placed us in this world, Both in blessings upon the protection of my religion, And the salvation of my soul, And the fulfillment of my needs, And the acceptance of my supplications, And the completion of Your bounty upon me, And the repelling of evil from me, And the clothing of well-being for me. And that You (azj) make me, by Your mercy, among those for whom You (azj) secured the Night of al-Qadr, and made it for him better than ‘a thousand months’ (Surah Al Qadr) in the greatest reward, the most noble reserves, the longest life, the best gratitude, and the continuity of ease. O’ Allah (swt), I also ask You (azj) by Your mercy, and Your bounty, and Your pardon, and Your blessings, and Your majesty, and Your ancient kindness and generosity, that You (azj) do not make this our last encounter with the Month of Ramadan, until You (azj) allow us to reach it again in the coming year in the best of states, and that You (azj) show me its crescent moon together with those who behold it and recognize it, in the fullest of Your well-being, the most gracious of Your blessings, the vastest of Your mercy, and the most abundant of Your allotment. O’ Allah (swt), O’ my Lord (azj), there is no Lord (azj) for me other than You (azj), do not make this farewell of mine a farewell of separation and extinction. And not the last of the covenant of encounter, until You (azj) show it to me again in the fullness of blessings and the best of hopes, while I remain in the finest state of loyalty to You (azj), ‘indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication’ (Surah Al Imran 3:38). O’ Allah (swt), hear my supplication, my humble entreaty, my submissiveness before You (azj), my brokenness, and my reliance upon You (azj). I am in full submission to You (azj), I seek no success, no well-being, no honor, and no attainment except through You (azj), and from You (azj). So bestow it upon me, Exalted is Your praise, and sanctified are Your names by allowing me to reach the Month of Ramadan again while I am safe from every disliked and feared thing, and from all calamities. All praise is due to Allah (swt), who aided us in the fasting of this month and its nightly standing, until He (azj) brought us to its final night.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْقُمِّيِّ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« فِي وَدَاعِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ قُلْتَ فِي كِتَابِكَ اَلْمُنْزَلِ عَلَى لِسَانِ نَبِيِّكَ اَلْمُرْسَلِ صَلَوَاتُكَ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ قَوْلُكَ حَقٌّ« شَهْرُ رَمَضٰانَ اَلَّذِي أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ اَلْقُرْآنُ وَ هَذَا شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ قَدْ تَصَرَّمَ فَأَسْأَلُكَ بِوَجْهِكَ اَلْكَرِيمِ وَ كَلِمَاتِكَ اَلتَّامَّةِ إِنْ كَانَ بَقِيَ عَلَيَّ ذَنْبٌ لَمْ تَغْفِرْهُ لِي أَوْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تُعَذِّبَنِي عَلَيْهِ أَوْ تُقَايِسَنِي بِهِ أَنْ يَطْلُعَ فَجْرُ هَذِهِ اَللَّيْلَةِ أَوْ يَتَصَرَّمَ هَذَا اَلشَّهْرُ إِلاَّ وَ قَدْ غَفَرْتَهُ لِي يَا أَرْحَمَ اَلرَّاحِمِينَ اَللَّهُمَّ لَكَ اَلْحَمْدُ بِمَحَامِدِكَ كُلِّهَا أَوَّلِهَا وَ آخِرِهَا مَا قُلْتَ لِنَفْسِكَ مِنْهَا وَ مَا قَالَ لَكَ اَلْخَلاَئِقُ اَلْحَامِدُونَ اَلْمُجْتَهِدُونَ اَلْمُعَدِّدُونَ اَلْمُؤْثِرُونَ فِي ذِكْرِكَ وَ اَلشُّكْرِ لَكَ اَلَّذِينَ أَعَنْتَهُمْ عَلَى أَدَاءِ حَقِّكَ مِنْ أَصْنَافِ خَلْقِكَ مِنَ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةِ اَلْمُقَرَّبِينَ وَ اَلنَّبِيِّينَ وَ اَلْمُرْسَلِينَ وَ أَصْنَافِ اَلنَّاطِقِينَ اَلْمُسَبِّحِينَ لَكَ مِنْ جَمِيعِ اَلْعَالَمِينَ عَلَى أَنَّكَ بَلَّغْتَنَا شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ وَ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ نِعَمِكَ وَ عِنْدَنَا مِنْ قَسْمِكَ وَ إِحْسَانِكَ وَ تَظَاهُرِ اِمْتِنَانِكَ بِذَلِكَ لَكَ مُنْتَهَى اَلْحَمْدِ اَلْخَالِدِ اَلدَّائِمِ اَلرَّاكِدِ اَلْمُخَلَّدِ اَلسَّرْمَدِ اَلَّذِي لاَ يَنْفَدُ طُولَ اَلْأَبَدِ جَلَّ ثَنَاؤُكَ أَعَنْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى قَضَيْتَ عَنَّا صِيَامَهُ وَ قِيَامَهُ مِنْ صَلاَةٍ وَ مَا كَانَ مِنَّا فِيهِ مِنْ بِرٍّ أَوْ شُكْرٍ أَوْ ذِكْرٍ اَللَّهُمَّ فَتَقَبَّلْهُ مِنَّا بِأَ حْسَنِ قَبُولِكَ وَ تَجَاوُزِكَ وَ عَفْوِكَ وَ صَفْحِكَ وَ غُفْرَانِكَ وَ حَقِيقَةِ رِضْوَانِكَ حَتَّى تُظْفِرَنَا فِيهِ بِكُلِّ خَيْرٍ مَطْلُوبٍ وَجَزِيلِ عَطَاءٍ مَوْهُوبٍ وَ تُؤْمِنَنَا فِيهِ مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ مَرْهُوبٍ وَذَنْبٍ مَكْسُوبٍ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ بِعَظِيمِ مَا سَأَلَكَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ خَلْقِكَ مِنْ كَرِيمِ أَسْمَائِكَ وَ جَزِيلِ ثَنَائِكَ وَ خَاصَّةِ دُعَائِكَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ شَهْرَنَا هَذَا أَعْظَمَ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ مَرَّ عَلَيْنَا مُنْذُ أَنْزَلْتَنَا إِلَى اَلدُّنْيَا بَرَكَةً فِي عِصْمَةِ دِينِي وَ خَلاَصِ نَفْسِي وَ قَضَاءِ حَاجَتِي وَ تَشْفِيعِي فِي مَسَائِلِي وَ تَمَامِ اَلنِّعْمَةِ عَلَيَّ وَ صَرْفِ اَلسُّوءِ عَنِّي وَ لِبَاسِ اَلْعَافِيَةِ لِي وَ أَنْ تَجْعَلَنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ مِمَّنْ حُزْتَ لَهُ لَيْلَةَ اَلْقَدْرِ وَ جَعَلْتَهَا لَهُ خَيْراً« مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ» فِي أَعْظَمِ اَلْأَجْرِ وَ كَرَائِمِ اَلذُّخْرِ وَ طُولِ اَلْعُمُرِ وَ حُسْنِ اَلشُّكْرِ وَ دَوَامِ اَلْيُسْرِ اَللَّهُمَّ وَ أَسْأَلُكَ بِرَحْمَتِكَ وَ طَوْلِكَ وَ عَفْوِكَ وَ نَعْمَائِكَ وَ جَلاَلِكَ وَ قَدِيمِ إِحْسَانِكَ وَ اِمْتِنَانِكَ أَنْ لاَ تَجْعَلَهُ آخِرَ اَلْعَهْدِ مِنَّا بِشَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ حَتَّى تُبَلِّغَنَاهُ مِنْ قَابِلٍ عَلَى أَحْسَنِ حَالٍ وَ تُعَرِّفَنِي هِلاَلَهُ مَعَ اَلنَّاظِرِينَ إِلَيْهِ وَ اَلْمُتَعَرِّفِينَ لَهُ فِي أَعْفَى عَافِيَتِكَ وَ أَنْعَمِ نِعْمَتِكَ وَ أَوْسَعِ رَحْمَتِكَ وَ أَجْزَلِ قَسْمِكَ اَللَّهُمَّ يَا رَبِّيَ اَلَّذِي لَيْسَ لِي رَبٌّ غَيْرُهُ لاَ يَكُونُ هَذَا اَلْوَدَاعُ مِنِّي وَدَاعَ فَنَاءٍ وَ لاَ آخِرَ اَلْعَهْدِ مِنَ اَللِّقَاءِ حَتَّى تُرِيَنِيهِ مِنْ قَابِلٍ فِي أَسْبَغِ اَلنِّعَمِ وَ أَفْضَلِ اَلرَّجَاءِ وَ أَنَا لَكَ عَلَى أَحْسَنِ اَلْوَفَاءِ« إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ اَلدُّعٰاءِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِسْمَعْ دُعَائِي وَ تَضَرُّعِي وَ تَذَلُّلِي لَكَ وَاِسْتِكَانَتِي وَ تَوَكُّلِي عَلَيْكَ وَأَنَا لَكَ سِلْمٌ لاَ أَرْجُو نَجَاحاً وَلاَ مُعَافَاةً وَلاَ تَشْرِيفاً وَلاَ تَبْلِيغاً إِلاَّ بِكَ وَ مِنْكَ فَامْنُنْ عَلَيَّ جَلَّ ثَنَاؤُكَ وَ تَقَدَّسَتْ أَسْمَاؤُكَ بِتَبْلِيغِي شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ وَ أَنَا مُعَافًى مِنْ كُلِّ مَكْرُوهٍ وَ مَحْذُورٍ مِنْ جَمِيعِ اَلْبَوَائِقِ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي أَعَانَنَا عَلَى صِيَامِ هَذَا اَلشَّهْرِ وَ قِيَامِهِ حَتَّى بَلَّغَنَا آخِرَ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْهُ»

items.e: Narrated by Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmari from Abdillah ibn Hammad al-Ansari from Abu Basir from a group among his companions from Sadan ibn Muslim from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: something similar to that, and he added in it: (The addition to the supplication) “O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by the most beloved of what You (azj) have been supplicated with, and the most pleasing of what You (azj) have been pleased with for (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that You (azj) bless (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and do not make my farewell to the Month of Ramadan, the farewell of departure from this world, nor the last of my worship of You (azj) in it, nor the last of my fasting for You (azj), and grant me the return to it, then the return to it, through Your mercy. O’ Guardian of the believers, and grant me success in the Night of al-Qadr and make it for me ‘better than a thousand months’ (Surah Al Qadr). O’ Lord (azj) of the worlds, O’ Lord (azj) of the Night of al-Qadr and the One who has made it better than ‘a thousand months’, O’ Lord (azj) of the night and the day, and the mountains and the seas, and the darknesses and the lights, and the earth and the sky. O’ Creator, O’ Fashioner, O’ Most Compassionate, O’ Most Bountiful, O’ Allah (swt), O’ All-Merciful, O’ Most Merciful, O’ Ever-Living, O’ Originator of the heavens and the earth, to You (azj) belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Attributes, the Majesty, and the Blessings. I ask You (azj) by Your Name: ‘In the name of Allah (swt), the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful’, to bless (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), And to place my name on this night among the fortunate ones, And my soul among the martyrs, And my good deeds in the highest of the high, And my misdeeds as forgiven. And to grant me certainty that directly touches my heart, And faith not tainted by doubt, And contentment with what You (azj) have allotted for me, And to grant me ‘good in this world and good in Hereafter’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:201). And that You (azj) protect me from ‘the punishment of Fire’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:201). O’ Allah (swt), place in what You (azj) decree and ordain from the determined matter, and in what You (azj) separate from the wise command on the Night of al-Qadr, in the decree that is not repelled, nor altered, nor changed, that You (azj) write me among the pilgrims of Your Sacred House, those whose Hajj is accepted, whose striving is appreciated, whose sins are forgiven, and whose misdeeds are atoned for. And place in what You (azj) decree and ordain that You (azj) set my neck free from the Fire, O’ Most Merciful of the merciful. O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj), and no servant asks anyone with the generosity and liberality like Yours, and I turn with longing to You (azj), and none is turned to, like You (azj). You (azj) are the one to whom the supplication of those who ask is directed, and the ultimate object of desire for those who seek. I ask You (azj) with the greatest of all requests, and the best of them, and the most successful of them, that which it befits the servants to ask You (azj) with. O’ Allah (swt), O’ Most Merciful, O’ Most Compassionate, And by Your Names those of them which I know and those which I do not know, And by Your Most Beautiful Names and Your Highest Attributes, And by Your blessings which cannot be counted, And by the noblest of Your Names in Your sight, and the most beloved to You (azj), And the most honorable in rank before You (azj), And the closest of them to You (azj) in means, And the greatest of them in reward from You (azj), And the swiftest of them in being answered by You (azj), And by Your hidden, treasured Name the Ever-Living, the Sustainer, the Greatest, the Most Glorious the Name which You (azj) love, and desire, and are pleased with when someone calls upon You (azj) by it, and You (azj) answer their supplication. And it is incumbent upon You (azj) not to disappoint one who asks of You (azj). And I ask You (azj) by every name that belongs to You (azj), And by your every name in the Torah, And by your every name in the Gospel, And by your every name in the Psalms, And by your every name in the Criterion (the Qur’an), And by every name with which those who bear Your Throne, have called upon You (azj). And by the angels of Your heavens, And the inhabitants of Your earth, whether prophet, or truthful one, or martyr, And by the right of those who turn toward You (azj) with longing, those who are drawn near to You (azj), those who seek refuge in You (azj). And by the right of those who reside near Your Sacred House pilgrims, and those performing umrah, and those sanctifying it, and those striving in Your path. And by the right of every servant who worships You (azj), whether on land, or sea, or plain, or mountain. I call upon You (azj) with the supplication of one whose need has intensified, whose sins are many, whose burden is great, whose effort is weak; the supplication of one who finds for himself no provider, no support for his weakness, no forgiver for his sins besides You (azj), fleeing to You (azj), seeking refuge with You (azj), devoted in worship to You (azj), neither arrogant nor disdainful, fearful, wretched, poor, and seeking protection with You (azj). I ask You (azj) by Your Might and Your Greatness. And by Your overwhelming power, And by Your authority, And by Your dominion, And by Your splendor, And by Your generosity, And by Your bounty, And by Your blessings, And by Your beauty, And by Your elegance, And by Your power over whatever You (azj) will from among Your creation, I call upon You (azj), O’ my Lord (azj), in fear and hope, in awe and in longing, with humility and devotion, with supplication and persistence, with insistence and pleading, in submission to You (azj), there is no God but You (azj), You (azj) alone, You (azj) have no partner. O’ Holy One, O’ Holy One, O’ Holy One, O’ Allah (swt), O’ Allah (swt), O’ Allah (swt), O’ All-Merciful, O’ All-Merciful, O’ All-Merciful, O’ Most Compassionate, O’ Most Compassionate, O’ Most Compassionate, O’ Lord, O’ Lord, O’ Lord I seek refuge in You (azj), O’ Allah (swt), the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, the Single, the Supreme, the Most Exalted. And I ask You (azj) by everything I have called upon You (azj) with, and by Your Names which fill all of Your dominions, that You (azj) bless (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and forgive me, and have mercy on me, and expand for me from Your great bounty, And accept from me the Month of Ramadan its fasting, its night prayers, its obligations, and its supererogatory acts and forgive me, And have mercy on me, and pardon me, And do not make it the last Month of Ramadan that I fasted for You (azj) and worshipped You (azj) in. And do not make my farewell to it the farewell of departure from this world. O’ Allah (swt), ordain for me from Your mercy, Your forgiveness, Your pleasure, and Your awe the best of what You (azj) have given to anyone who worshipped You (azj) in it. O’ Allah (swt), so do not make me the most deprived among those who asked You (azj) during it, And make me among those whom You (azj) have freed in this month from the Fire, And forgiven for them what has passed of their sins and what is yet to come, And for whom You (azj) have decreed the best of what was hoped and longed for from You O’ Most Merciful of the merciful. O’ Allah (swt), grant me the opportunity to return to fasting it for You (azj), and worshipping You (azj) in it, And make me among those whom You (azj) have written in this month as the pilgrims of Your Sacred House, those whose Hajj is accepted, whose sins are forgiven, and whose deeds are accepted. Ameen, ameen, ameen, O’ Lord (azj) of the worlds. O’ Allah (swt), do not leave for me in it, any sin but that You (azj) forgive it, nor any misdeed but that You (azj) erase it, nor any stumble but that You (azj) lift it, nor any debt but that You (azj) repay it, nor any poverty but that You (azj) enrich it, for indeed, in Your generosity, Your pardon, and Your bounty, there is vastness for the forgiveness of our sins. So forgive us, overlook us, and do not punish us for them, O’ Most Merciful of the merciful. O’ Allah (swt), honor me in this gathering of mine, with an honor after which You (azj) will never disgrace me, And grant me a dignity after which You (azj) will never humiliate me, And grant me well-being with a well-being after which You (azj) will never afflict me, And raise me with an elevation after which You (azj) will never bring me down. And turn away from me the evil of every rebellious devil, And the evil of every stubborn tyrant, And the evil of every near or distant one, And the evil of every small or great (being), And the evil of every creature You (azj) are the One who ‘holds it by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path’ (Surah Hud 11:56). O’ Allah (swt), whatever is in my heart of doubt, or uncertainty, or denial, or despair, or grief, or frivolity, or arrogance, or joy, or pride, or hypocrisy, or showing off, or seeking reputation, or division, or insincerity, or disbelief, or immorality, or disobedience, or anything through which You (azj) are not pleased with a friend of Yours, I ask You (azj) to erase it from my heart and replace it with faith in You (azj), contentment with Your decree, loyalty to Your covenant, fear of You (azj), detachment from the world, desire for what is with You (azj), trust in You (azj), tranquility toward You (azj), and a sincere repentance to You (azj). O’ Allah (swt), if You (azj) have already enabled us to reach it, then (accept it); but if not, then delay our lives until the coming year, so that You (azj) enable us to reach it, with ease from You (azj) and well-being, O’ Most Merciful of the merciful. And may Allah (swt) send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and his pure, purified, virtuous family (a.s), and grant them much and noble peace and may the mercy of Allah (swt) and His (azj) blessings be upon them.”
items.o: وَ رَوَى إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْأَحْمَرِيُّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ اَلْأَنْصَارِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ جَمَاعَةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ وَ زَادَ فِيهِ« اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ بِأَحَبِّ مَا دُعِيتَ بِهِ وَ أَرْضَى مَا رَضِيتَ بِهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ لاَ تَجْعَلْ وَدَاعِي شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ وَدَاعَ خُرُوجِي مِنَ اَلدُّنْيَا وَ لاَ وَدَاعَ آخِرِ عِبَادَتِكَ فِيهِ وَ لاَ آخِرَ صَوْمِي لَكَ وَ اُرْزُقْنِي اَلْعَوْدَ فِيهِ ثُمَّ اَلْعَوْدَ فِيهِ بِرَحْمَتِكَ يَا وَلِيَّ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ وَفِّقْنِي لِلَيْلَةِ اَلْقَدْرِ وَ اِجْعَلْهَا لِي خَيْراً« مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ» يَا رَبَّ اَلْعَالَمِينَ يَا رَبَّ لَيْلَةِ اَلْقَدْرِ وَ جَاعِلَهَا خَيْراً مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ رَبَّ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ اَلْجِبَالِ وَ اَلْبِحَارِ وَ اَلظُّلَمِ وَ اَلْأَنْوَارِ وَ اَلْأَرْضِ وَاَلسَّمَاءِ يَا بَارِئُ يَا مُصَوِّرُ يَا حَنَّانُ يَا مَنَّانُ يَا اَللَّهُ يَا رَحْمَانُ يَا رَحِيمُ يَا قَيُّومُ يَا بَدِيعَ اَلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَاَلْأَرْضِ لَكَ اَلْأَسْمَاءُ اَلْحُسْنَى وَ اَلْأَمْثَالُ اَلْعُلْيَا وَ اَلْكِبْرِيَاءُ وَ اَلْآلاَءُ أَسْأَلُكَ بِاسْمِكَ« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ» أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ اِسْمِي تُبَلِّغَنَاهُ فِي يُسْرٍ مِنْكَ وَ عَافِيَةٍ يَا أَرْحَمَ اَلرَّاحِمِينَ وَ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِهِ اَلطَّيِّبِينَ اَلطَّاهِرِينَ اَلْأَخْيَارِ وَ سَلَّمَ كَثِيراً طَيِّباً وَ رَحْمَةُ اَللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Abu Usamah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the ‘takbir’ in the two Eid prayers. Imam (a.s) said: “Seven and five.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The prayer of the two Eids is an obligation (faridah), and the prayer of ‘al-Kusuf’ (prayer of eclipse) is an obligation.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ سَبْعٌ وَخَمْسٌ وَقَالَ« صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فَرِيضَةٌ وَصَلاَةُ اَلْكُسُوفِ فَرِيضَةٌ».
items.h: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr and Fadalah from Jamil, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the takbir in the two Eid prayers. Imam (a.s) said: “Seven and five.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The prayer of the two Eids is an obligation (faridah).” I asked Imam (a.s) what is recited in them. Imam (a.s) said: “’By the sun and its morning brightness’ (Surah Ash-Shams) and ‘Has there come to you the report of the overwhelming event’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah) and those (Surah) like them.
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ« سَبْعٌ وَخَمْسٌ» وَقَالَ« صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فَرِيضَةٌ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ مَا يُقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا قَالَ«« وَاَلشَّمْسِ وَضُحٰاهٰا» وَ« هَلْ أَتٰاكَ حَدِيثُ اَلْغٰاشِيَةِ» وَ أَشْبَاهُهُمَا»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The prayer of the two Eids is two rak’ahs, without adhan and without iqamah. There is nothing before them nor after them (in terms of prayer).”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ رَكْعَتَانِ بِلاَ أَذَانٍ وَ لاَ إِقَامَةٍ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا شَيْءٌ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mualla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha from Hammad ibn Uthman from Mamar ibn Yahya from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “There is no prayer on the Day of Fitr and the Day of Adha except with an (just) imam.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مَعْمَرِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ صَلاَةَ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى إِلاَّ مَعَ إِمَامٍ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Whoever does not pray with the (just) imam in congregation on the Day of Eid, then there is no prayer for him, and no make-up (qada) is required of him.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ لَمْ يُصَلِّ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ يَوْمَ اَلْعِيدِ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ وَ لاَ قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ»

items.e: And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama’ah from Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There is no prayer on the two Eids except with a (just) imam. But if you pray alone, then there is no harm.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ صَلاَةَ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ إِلاَّ مَعَ إِمَامٍ فَإِنْ صَلَّيْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»

items.e: And from him, from Safwan from al-Ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, who said: I asked Imam (a.s) about the prayer on the Day of Fitr and the Day of Adha. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no prayer except with a (just) imam.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ صَلاَةٌ إِلاَّ مَعَ إِمَامٍ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Zurarah, who said that Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “There is no adhan and no iqamah on the Day of Fitr and the Day of Adha. Their ‘adhan’ is the rising of the sun when it rises, they go out. And there is no prayer before them nor after them. And whoever does not pray with the (just) imam in congregation, there is no prayer for him, and no make-up (qada) is required of him.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: «لَيْسَ فِي يَوْمِ اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى أَذَانٌ وَ لاَ إِقَامَةٌ أَذَانُهُمَا طُلُوعُ اَلشَّمْسِ إِذَا طَلَعَتْ خَرَجُوا وَ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا صَلاَةٌ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يُصَلِّ مَعَ إِمَامٍ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ وَ لاَ قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ»

items.e: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmari from al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalaf from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The prayer of the two Eids with the (just) imam is a sunnah, and there is no prayer before it nor after it on that day until midday (zawal). And if you missed the witr in your night, you may make it up after zawal.”
items.o: إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْأَحْمَرِيُّ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ أَبِي خَلَفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ سُنَّةٌ وَ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهَا صَلاَةٌ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ إِلَى اَلزَّوَالِ فَإِنْ فَاتَكَ اَلْوَتْرُ فِي لَيْلَتِكَ قَضَيْتَهُ بَعْدَ اَلزَّوَالِ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Muawiyah, said: I asked Imam (a.s) about the prayer of the two Eids. Imam (a.s) said: “Two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them nor after them, and there is no adhan nor iqamah in them. In them, twelve takbirs are recited. He begins, says the takbir, and opens the prayer, then recites the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah), then recites ‘By the sun and its morning brightness’ (Surah Ash-Shams), then says five takbirs, Then says a takbir and goes into rukuh, so he bows with the seventh (takbir). Then he performs two prostrations (sajdatayn), then he stands and recites the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah), and ‘Has there come to you the report of the overwhelming event’ (Surah Al-Ghashiyah), then he says four takbirs, then performs two prostrations, and then recites the tashahhud.” Imam (a.s) said: “And likewise did the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, do. The sermon (khutbah) is after the prayer. It was Uthman (third oppressor), who innovated placing the sermon before the prayer. And when the imam (of prayer) delivers the sermon, he should sit briefly between the two sermons. It is proper for the imam (of prayer) to wear a cloak (burd) on the two Eid days, and to wear a turban, whether it is winter or summer, and to go out to an open area where he can see the horizons of the sky. He should not pray on a mat (hasir), nor prostrate on it. And indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to go out to al-Baqi and pray with the people.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فَقَالَ« رَكْعَتَانِ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا شَيْءٌ وَ لَيْسَ فِيهِمَا أَذَانٌ وَ لاَ إِقَامَةٌ يُكَبِّرُ فِيهِمَا اِثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً يَبْدَأُ فَيُكَبِّرُ وَ يَفْتَتِحُ اَلصَّلاَةَ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ« وَ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحٰاهٰا» ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ خَمْسَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ فَيَرْكَعُ فَيَكُونُ يَرْكَعُ بِالسَّابِعَةِ وَ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيَقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ« هَلْ أَتٰاكَ حَدِيثُ اَلْغٰاشِيَةِ» ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ أَرْبَعَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ وَ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيْنِ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ» قَالَ« وَ كَذَلِكَ صَنَعَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ اَلْخُطْبَةُ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ إِنَّمَا أَحْدَثَ اَلْخُطْبَةَ قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ عُثْمَانُ وَإِذَا خَطَبَ اَلْإِمَامُ فَلْيَقْعُدْ بَيْنَ اَلْخُطْبَتَيْنِ قَلِيلاً وَ يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَلْبَسَ يَوْمَ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ بُرْداً وَ يَعْتَمَّ شَاتِياً كَانَ أَوْ قَائِظاً وَ يَخْرُجَ إِلَى اَلْبَرِّ حَيْثُ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى آفَاقِ اَلسَّمَاءِ وَ لاَ يُصَلِّيَ عَلَى حَصِيرٍ وَ لاَ يَسْجُدَ عَلَيْهِ وَ قَدْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يَخْرُجُ إِلَى اَلْبَقِيعِ فَيُصَلِّي بِالنَّاسِ»

items.e: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding the Eid prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “He says the takbir, then recites, then says five takbirs, and performs ‘qunut’ between every two takbirs. Then he says the seventh takbir, then bows (rukuh) with it, then prostrates (sujud), then stands for the second unit, recites, then says four takbirs, and performs qunut between every two takbirs, then says a takbir and bows with it.”
items.o: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ« يُكَبِّرُ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ خَمْساً وَ يَقْنُتُ بَيْنَ كُلِّ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ اَلسَّابِعَةَ ثُمَّ يَرْكَعُ بِهَا ثُمَّ يَسْجُدُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَيَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ أَرْبَعاً فَيَقْنُتُ بَيْنَ كُلِّ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ وَ يَرْكَعُ بِهَا»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Sabbah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the takbir in the two Eids. Imam (a.s) said: “Twelve takbirs; seven in the first unit, and five in the last (unit).”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلصَّبَّاحِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ« اِثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً سَبْعٌ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَ خَمْسٌ فِي اَلْأَخِيرَةِ»

items.e: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding the Eid prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Say six takbirs, and bow with the seventh (takbir). Then stand for the second unit, recite, then say four takbirs, and bow with the fifth. And the sermon is after the prayer.”
items.o: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ اِبْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ« كَبِّرْ سِتَّ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ وَ اِرْكَعْ بِالسَّابِعَةِ ثُمَّ قُمْ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَاقْرَأْ ثُمَّ كَبِّرْ أَرْبَعاً وَ اِرْكَعْ بِالْخَامِسَةِ وَ اَلْخُطْبَةُ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ»

items.e: And from him, from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: I heard Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) say: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to wear a turban (i'timmah) on the two Eids, whether it was winter or summer, and He (saws) would wear his coat of mail (dir), and likewise it is proper for the (just) imam to do so, and He (saws) would recite aloud (jahr') in the prayer just as he recites aloud in the Friday prayer.”
items.o: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يَعْتَمُّ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ شَاتِياً كَانَ أَوْ قَائِظاً وَ يَلْبَسُ دِرْعَهُ وَ كَذَلِكَ يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ وَ يَجْهَرُ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ كَمَا يَجْهَرُ فِي اَلْجُمُعَةِ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Hasan from Zurah ibn Muhammad from Sama’ah, who said: I asked Imam (a.s) about the prayer on the Day of Fitr. Imam (a.s) said: “Two rak’ahs without adhan and without iqamah, and it is proper for the Imam to pray before the sermon. The takbirs in the first rak’ah he says six takbirs, then recites, then says the seventh takbir and bows with it. So that is seven takbirs. Then he stands for the second (rak’ah), and recites, and when he finishes the recitation, he says four takbirs and bows with it. And it is proper for him to humble himself between every two takbirs and to supplicate to Allah (swt). This is in the prayer of Fitr and Adha equally, and it is the same in all the cities except on the Day of Adha in Mina, for on that day there is neither prayer nor takbir.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ فَقَالَ« رَكْعَتَيْنِ بِغَيْرِ أَذَانٍ وَ لاَ إِقَامَةٍ وَ يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ قَبْلَ اَلْخُطْبَةِ وَ اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى يُكَبِّرُ سِتّاًثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ اَلسَّابِعَةَ ثُمَّ يَرْكَعُ بِهَا فَتِلْكَ سَبْعُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَيَقْرَأُ فَإِذَا فَرَغَ مِنَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ كَبَّرَ أَرْبَعاً وَ يَرْكَعُ بِهَا وَ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَتَضَرَّعَ بَيْنَ كُلِّ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ وَ يَدْعُوَ اَللَّهَ هَذَا فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ سَوَاءً وَ هُوَ فِي اَلْأَمْصَارِ كُلِّهَا إِلاَّ يَوْمَ اَلْأَضْحَى بِمِنًى فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ يَوْمَئِذٍ صَلاَةٌ وَ لاَ تَكْبِيرٌ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The takbirs in the two Eids are seven in the first (rak’ah) before the recitation, and in the second (rak’ah) five after the recitation.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فِي اَلْأُولَى سَبْعٌ قَبْلَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ وَ فِي اَلْأَخِيرَةِ خَمْسٌ بَعْدَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ

items.e: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ismail ibn Sa’ad al-Ashari from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, said: He (narrator) said: “I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s) about the takbir in the two Eids.” Imam (a.s) said: “The takbir in the first (rak’ah) is seven takbirs before the recitation, and in the second (rak’ah) it is five takbirs after the recitation.”
items.o: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ «اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي اَلْأُولَى سَبْعُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ قَبْلَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ وَ فِي اَلْأَخِيرَةِ خَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa from Shuayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The takbir in (the prayers of) al-Fitr and al-Adha is twelve takbirs. In the first (rak’ah), he says one takbir, then he recites, then after the recitation he says five takbirs, and with the seventh takbir, he bows (in ruku). Then he rises for the second (rak’ah), recites, then says four takbirs, and with the fifth he bows (in rukuh).” And Imam (a.s) said: “It is appropriate for the Imam to wear a fine garment (hullah) and to wear a turban (imamah), whether it is winter or summer.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى اِثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً يُكَبِّرُ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَاحِدَةً ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ بَعْدَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ خَمْسَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ وَاَلسَّابِعَةُ يَرْكَعُ بِهَا ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَيَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ أَرْبَعاً وَاَلْخَامِسَةُ يَرْكَعُ بِهَا» وَقَالَ« يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَلْبَسَ حُلَّةً وَ يَعْتَمَّ شَاتِياً كَانَ أَوْ صَائِفاً»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Yaqub ibn Yaqtin who said: I asked the Servant (of Allah (swt)), Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) peace be upon him, about the takbir in the two Eids, whether it is before or after the recitation and how many takbirs are in the first and in the second (rak’ah), and about the supplication between them, and whether there is qunut in them or not. Imam (a.s) said: “The takbir of the two Eids in prayer is before the sermon. He pronounces a takbirah with which he opens the prayer, then he recites, then he says five takbirs and makes supplication between them, then he says another takbirah and bows with it so that is seven takbirs including the one with which he began. Then in the second (rak’ah), he says five takbirs, he stands and recites, then says four takbirs and supplicates between them, then says the fifth takbirah.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلْعَبْدَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ أَ قَبْلَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ أَوْ بَعْدَهَا وَكَمْ عَدَدُ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَفِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ وَاَلدُّعَاءُ بَيْنَهُمَا وَهَلْ فِيهِمَا قُنُوتٌ أَمْ لاَ فَقَالَ« تَكْبِيرُ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ لِلصَّلاَةِ قَبْلَ اَلْخُطْبَةِ يُكَبِّرُ تَكْبِيرَةً يَفْتَتِحُ بِهَا اَلصَّلاَةَ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ خَمْساً وَ يَدْعُو بَيْنَهُمَا ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ أُخْرَى وَ يَرْكَعُ بِهَا فَذَلِكَ سَبْعُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ بِالَّتِي اِفْتَتَحَ بِهَا ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ خَمْساً يَقُومُ فَيَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ أَرْبَعاً وَ يَدْعُو بَيْنَهُنَّ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ اَلتَّكْبِيرَةَ اَلْخَامِسَةَ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ahmad ibn Abdillah al-Qarawi from Aban ibn Uthman from Ismail al-Jufi from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said regarding the Eid prayer: “He pronounces a single takbirah with which he opens the prayer, then he recites the ‘Umm al-Kitab’ (Surah Al Fatihah) and a surah. Then he says five takbirs, and performs ‘qunut’ between them. Then he says one takbirah and bows with it. Then he stands and recites the ‘Umm al-Kitab’ (Surah Al Fatihah) and a surah. In first (rak’ah), he recites ‘Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High’ (Surah Al-A’la) and in second (rak’ah), ‘By the sun and its morning brightness’ (Surah Ash-Shams). Then he says four takbirs and does qunut between them, then bows with the fifth one.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْقَرَوِيِّ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلْجُعْفِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ« يُكَبِّرُ وَاحِدَةً يَفْتَتِحُ بِهَا اَلصَّلاَةَ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ أُمَّ اَلْكِتَابِ وَسُورَةً ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ خَمْساً يَقْنُتُ بَيْنَهُنَّ ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ وَاحِدَةً وَ يَرْكَعُ بِهَا ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيَقْرَأُ أُمَّ اَلْقُرْآنِ وَ سُورَةً يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْأُولَى« سَبِّحِ اِسْمَ رَبِّكَ اَلْأَعْلَى» وَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ« وَ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحٰاهٰا» ثُمَّ يُكَبِّرُ أَرْبَعاً وَ يَقْنُتُ بَيْنَهُنَّ ثُمَّ يَرْكَعُ بِالْخَامِسَةِ»

items.e: From him, from Abdillah ibn Bahr from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the takbir in al-Fitr and al-Adha. Imam (a.s) said: “Begin and say one takbirah, then recite, then say five takbirs after the recitation, then bow with the seventh. Then stand and recite, then say four takbirs, then bow with the fifth.”
items.o: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بَحْرٍ عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى فَقَالَ« اِبْدَأْ فَكَبِّرْ تَكْبِيرَةً ثُمَّ تَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ تُكَبِّرُ بَعْدَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ خَمْسَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ ثُمَّ تَرْكَعُ بِالسَّابِعَةِ ثُمَّ تَقُومُ فَتَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ تُكَبِّرُ أَرْبَعَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ ثُمَّ تَرْكَعُ بِالْخَامِسَةِ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Sabbah who said: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the takbir in the two Eids. Imam (a.s) said: “Twelve seven in the first and five in the last. So when you stand for the prayer, say one takbirah, and say: ‘I bear witness that there is no God but Allah (swt), alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) is His (azj) servant and His (azj) messenger. O’ Allah (swt), You (azj) are worthy of majesty and greatness, and worthy of generosity and might, and power and authority and honor. I ask You (azj) on this day which You (azj) have made a feast for the Muslims and a treasure and increase for (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, I ask You (azj) to bless (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws). And that You (azj) send blessings upon Your nearest angels and Your commissioned prophets, and that You (azj) forgive us and all the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) for the best of what Your commissioned servants have asked You (azj) for, and I seek refuge in You (azj) from the worst of what Your sincere servants have sought refuge from. Allah (swt) is the Greatest, the First of all things and their Last, the Originator of all things and their End, the Knower of all things and their Return, and the Destination of all things is to Him (azj) and their Recourse, the Manager of affairs, and the Resurrector of ‘those who are in the graves’ (Surah Al-Adiyat 100:9). Allah (swt) is the Accepter of deeds, the Originator of the hidden things, the Revealer of secrets Allah (swt) is the Greatest, the One of immense dominion, severe in might, Living who does not die, Everlasting who does not vanish, “When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: Be! and it is.” (Surah Al Imran 3:47) Allah (swt) is the Greatest, voices are humbled before You (azj), faces submit to You (azj), eyes are bewildered before You (azj), tongues fall short of expressing Your greatness, all forelocks are in Your hand, and the measures of all matters are in Your care. No one decides in them except You (azj), and nothing of them is completed without You (azj). Allah (swt) is the Greatest Your protection encompasses all things. And Your might has overpowered all things, and Your command has penetrated all things, and all things stand by You (azj), and all things have humbled themselves before Your greatness, and all things have been subdued by Your might, and all things have submitted to Your power, and all things have yielded to Your sovereignty. Allah (swt) is the Greatest.” Then he recites ‘al-Hamd’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ (Surah Al-A’la), and he says the seventh takbirah and bows, and prostrates, and then rises and recites ‘al-Hamd’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘By the sun and its brightness’ (Surah Ash-Shams), and he says: ‘Allah (swt) is the Greatest. I bear witness that there is no God but Allah (swt), alone, with no partner, and that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) is His (azj) servant and messenger. O’ Allah (swt), You (azj) are worthy of majesty.’”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلصَّبَّاحِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فَقَالَ« اِثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ سَبْعٌ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَ خَمْسٌ فِي اَلْأَخِيرَةِ فَإِذَا قُمْتَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَكَبِّرْ وَاحِدَةً تَقُولُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ اَللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ أَهْلُ اَلْكِبْرِيَاءِ وَ اَلْعَظَمَةِ وَ أَهْلُ اَلْجُودِ وَ اَلْجَبَرُوتِ وَ اَلْقُدْرَةِ وَ اَلسُّلْطَانِ وَ اَلْعِزَّةِ أَسْأَلُكَ فِي هَذَا اَلْيَوْمِ اَلَّذِي جَعَلْتَهُ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ عِيداً وَ لِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ذُخْراً وَ مَزِيداً أَسْأَلُكَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مَلاَئِكَتِكَ اَلْمُقَرَّبِينَ وَ أَنْبِيَائِكَ اَلْمُرْسَلِينَ وَ أَنْ تَغْفِرَ لَنَا وَ لِجَمِيعِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ اَلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ اَلْمُسْلِمَاتِ اَلْأَحْيَاءِ مِنْهُمْ وَ اَلْأَمْوَاتِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ مَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادُكَ اَلْمُرْسَلُونَ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا عَاذَ بِهِ عِبَادُكَ اَلْمُخْلَصُونَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ أَوَّلُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَ آخِرُهُ وَ بَدِيعُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَ مُنْتَهَاهُ وَ عَالِمُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَ مَعَادُهُ وَ مَصِيرُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ إِلَيْهِ وَ مَرَدُّهُ وَ مُدَبِّرُ اَلْأُمُورِ وَ بَاعِثُ« مَنْ فِي اَلْقُبُورِ» قَابِلُ اَلْأَعْمَالِ مُبْدِئُ اَلْخَفِيَّاتِ مُعْلِنُ اَلسَّرَائِرِ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ عَظِيمُ اَلْمَلَكُوتِ شَدِيدُ اَلْجَبَرُوتِ حَيٌّ لاَ يَمُوتُ دَائِمٌ لاَ يَزُولُ« إِذٰا قَضىٰ أَمْراً فَإِنَّمٰا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ» اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ خَشَعَتْ لَكَ اَلْأَصْوَاتُ وَ عَنَتْ لَكَ اَلْوُجُوهُ وَ حَارَتْ دُونَكَ اَلْأَبْصَارُ وَ كَلَّتِ اَلْأَلْسُنُ عَنْ عَظَمَتِكَ وَ اَلنَّوَاصِي كُلُّهَا بِيَدِكَ وَ مَقَادِيرُ اَلْأُمُورِ كُلِّهَا إِلَيْكَ لاَ يَقْضِي فِيهَا غَيْرُكَ وَ لاَ يَتِمُّ مِنْهَا شَيْءٌ دُونَكَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ أَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ حِفْظُكَ وَ قَهَرَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِزُّكَ وَ نَفَذَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَمْرُكَ وَ قَامَ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ بِكَ وَ تَوَاضَعَ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ لِعَظَمَتِكَ وَ ذَلَّ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ لِعِزَّتِكَ وَ اِسْتَسْلَمَ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ لِقُدْرَتِكَ وَ خَضَعَ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ لِمُلْكِكَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَ يَقْرَأُ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« سَبِّحِ اِسْمَ رَبِّكَ اَلْأَعْلَى» وَ يُكَبِّرُ اَلسَّابِعَةَ وَ يَرْكَعُ وَ يَسْجُدُ وَ يَقُومُ وَ يَقْرَأُ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« اَلشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحٰاهٰا» وَ يَقُولُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ اَللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ أَهْلُ اَلْكِبْرِيَاءِ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah: Abd al-Malik ibn Ayan asked Aba Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer on the two Eid days. Imam (a.s) said: “The prayer in both is the same. The Imam pronounces the takbirah of the prayer while standing, just as he does in the obligatory prayer, then adds in the first rak’ah three takbirs, and in the second three as well, excluding the takbirah of the prayer, the bowing, and the prostration. If he wills, (he may do) three and five, and if he wills, five and seven, as long as he joins them to make an odd number (witr).”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ: أَنَّ عَبْدَ اَلْمَلِكِ بْنَ أَعْيَنَ سَأَلَ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فَقَالَ« اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيهِمَا سَوَاءٌ يُكَبِّرُ اَلْإِمَامُ تَكْبِيرَةَ اَلصَّلاَةِ قَائِماً كَمَا يَصْنَعُ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ ثُمَّ يَزِيدُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى ثَلاَثَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ وَ فِي اَلْأُخْرَى ثَلاَثاً سِوَى تَكْبِيرَةِ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ إِنْ شَاءَ ثَلاَثاً وَ خَمْساً وَ إِنْ شَاءَ خَمْساً وَ سَبْعاً بَعْدَ أَنْ يُلْحِقَ ذَلِكَ إِلَى وَتْرٍ»

items.e: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja’far from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who said: Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Eid prayer with the (just) imam is a sunnah, and there is no prayer before it nor after it on that day until midday (zawal).”
items.o: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ سُنَّةٌ وَ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهَا صَلاَةٌ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ إِلَى اَلزَّوَالِ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Uthman from Sama’ah from Abi Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There is no (prescribed) prayer on the two Eids except with the (just) imam. But if you pray alone, then there is no harm.” And I asked Imam (a.s) about eating before going out on the day of Eid. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes and if you do not eat, then there is no harm.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ صَلاَةَ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ إِلاَّ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ إِنْ صَلَّيْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْأَكْلِ قَبْلَ اَلْخُرُوجِ يَوْمَ اَلْعِيدِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَأْكُلْ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»

items.e: Sa’ad from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Muawiyah ibn Hakim from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah who said: Some of our companions narrated to me. He said: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer of al-Fitr and al-Adha. Imam (a.s) said: “Pray them as two rak’ahs, whether in congregation or individually, and say takbir seven times (in the first unit) and five times (in the second unit).”
items.o: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى فَقَالَ« صَلِّهِمَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ وَ غَيْرِ جَمَاعَةٍ وَ كَبِّرْ سَبْعاً وَ خَمْساً»

items.e: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Abi al-Bakhtari from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever misses the Eid prayer, let him pray four (rak’ahs).”
items.o: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ فَاتَتْهُ صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدِ فَلْيُصَلِّ أَرْبَعاً»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from al-Ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), who said: I asked Imam (a.s) about the prayer on the Day of Fitr and the Day of Adha. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no prayer except with the Imam.”
items.o: الحسين بن سعيد عن صفوان عن العلا عن محمد بن مسلم عن أحدهما قال سألته عن الصلاة يوم الفطر والاضحى فقال ليس صلاة إلا مع الامام

items.e: Ali ibn Hatim from al-Husayn ibn Ali from his father from Fadalah from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever does not attend the public congregation of people on the two Eids, let him perform ghusl, and apply fragrance with whatever he finds, and let him pray alone, just as he would pray in congregation.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Take your adornment at every masjid” (Surah Al-A’raf 7:31), And Imam (a.s) said: “(this applies to) The two Eids and Jumu’ah (Friday).”
items.o: عَلِيُّ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ لَمْ يَشْهَدْ جَمَاعَةَ اَلنَّاسِ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فَلْيَغْتَسِلْ وَ يَتَطَيَّبُ بِمَا وَجَدَ وَ لْيُصَلِّ وَحْدَهُ كَمَا يُصَلِّي فِي اَلْجَمَاعَةِ» وَ قَالَ«« خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ»» قَالَ« اَلْعِيدَانِ وَ اَلْجُمُعَةُ»

items.e: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: (A similar narration) And Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) added, saying: “On the Day of Arafah, they gather without an Imam in the cities ('amsar') to supplicate to Allah (swt), the Exalted, the Mighty and Majestic.”
items.o: وَرَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: مِثْلَهُ وَ زَادَ وَ قَالَ« فِي يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ يَجْتَمِعُونَ بِغَيْرِ إِمَامٍ فِي اَلْأَمْصَارِ يَدْعُونَ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ»

items.e: And from him, from al-Hasan from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who does not go out on the Day of Fitr and the Day of Adha, does he have to pray alone? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
items.o: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لاَ يَخْرُجُ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى أَ عَلَيْهِ صَلاَةٌ وَحْدَهُ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ»

items.e: And from him, from Umar ibn Ja’far who said: Abdillah ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Yaqub from Mansur from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “My father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) became ill on the Day of Adha, so he prayed two rak’ahs in his house, then offered the sacrifice.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَرِضَ أَبِي يَوْمَ اَلْأَضْحَى فَصَلَّى فِي بَيْتِهِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ ضَحَّى»

items.e: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: I (Zurarah) asked: “(If) I caught the imam (of prayer) while he was delivering the sermon.” Imam (a.s) said: “You sit until he (imam of prayer)) finishes his sermon, then you stand and pray.” I asked: “Should I begin with making up the prayer (qadah) or start with my own prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather start with your own prayer and this ruling applies only in this prayer.” I asked: “Then what if I catch part of the obligatory prayer with the imam (of prayer) and then complete the rest afterward?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for what you catch from the obligatory prayer, it is the beginning of your prayer, and what you make up is its end.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ أَدْرَكْتُ اَلْإِمَامَ عَلَى اَلْخُطْبَةِ قَالَ قَالَ« تَجْلِسُ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ مِنْ خُطْبَتِهِ ثُمَّ تَقُومُ فَتُصَلِّي» قُلْتُ اَلْقَضَاءُ أَوَّلُ صَلاَتِي أَوْ آخِرُهَا قَالَ« لاَ بَلْ أَوَّلُهَا وَ لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ فِي هَذِهِ اَلصَّلاَةِ» قُلْتُ فَمَا أَدْرَكْتُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ مَا قَضَيْتُ قَالَ« أَمَّا مَا أَدْرَكْتَ مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَهُوَ أَوَّلُ صَلاَتِكَ وَ مَا قَضَيْتَ فَآخِرُهَا»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr from Asim from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) narrates: “The people said to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, ‘Will you not appoint a man to lead the prayer on the two Eids?’” Imam Ali (a.s) said: “I will not go against the Sunnah.”
items.o: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَاصِمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« قَالَ اَلنَّاسُ لِأَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ لاَ تُخَلِّفُ رَجُلاً يُصَلِّي فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فَقَالَ« لاَ أُخَالِفُ اَلسُّنَّةَ»»

items.e: And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama’ah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “To eat before going out on the day of Eid is permissible and if you do not eat, there is no harm.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْأَ كْلُ قَبْلَ اَلْخُرُوجِ يَوْمَ اَلْعِيدِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَأْكُلْ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kallub from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: ‘When two Eids coincide for the people on the same day, it is appropriate for the Imam to say in his first sermon: ‘Two Eids have come together for you today, so I will pray them both together. Whoever's dwelling is far and wishes to leave after one of them, I have granted him permission to do so.’”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلْخَشَّابِ عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ كَلُّوبٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا اِجْتَمَعَ عِيدَانِ لِلنَّاسِ فِي يَوْمٍ وَاحِدٍ فَإِنَّهُ يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ فِي خُطْبَتِهِ اَلْأُولَى أَنَّهُ قَدِ اِجْتَمَعَ لَكُمْ عِيدَانِ فَأَنَا أُصَلِّيهِمَا جَمِيعاً فَمَنْ كَانَ مَكَانُهُ قَاصِياً فَأَحَبَّ أَنْ يَنْصَرِفَ عَنِ اَلْآخَرِ فَقَدْ أَذِنْتُ لَهُ

items.e: And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from al-Nawfali from al-Sukuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them, who said: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, forbade that weapons be brought out on the two Eids, except in the case of an evident enemy.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« نَهَى اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ اَلسِّلاَحُ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَدُوٌّ ظَاهِرٌ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban ibn Uthman from Salamah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Two Eids coincided during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, so Imam Ali (a.s) addressed the people and said: ‘This is a day in which two Eids have come together. So whoever wishes to perform the congregational prayer with us, let him do so, and whoever does not, then indeed there is a concession for him’ (meaning whoever is staying at a distance).”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَلَمَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اِجْتَمَعَ عِيدَانِ عَلَى عَهْدِ أَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَخَطَبَ اَلنَّاسَ فَقَالَ« هَذَا يَوْمٌ اِجْتَمَعَ فِيهِ عِيدَانِ فَمَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُجَمِّعَ مَعَنَا فَلْيَفْعَلْ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ فَإِنَّ لَهُ رُخْصَةً» يَعْنِي مَنْ كَانَ مُتَنَحِّياً»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who raised it (in isnad) to Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Sunnah for the people of the cities is that they should go out from their cities on the two Eids, except for the people of Makkah, for they perform the prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلسُّنَّةُ عَلَى أَهْلِ اَلْأَمْصَارِ أَنْ يَبْرُزُوا مِنْ أَمْصَارِهِمْ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ إِلاَّ أَهْلَ مَكَّةَ فَإِنَّهُمْ يُصَلُّونَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ»

items.e: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There are two rak’ahs from the Sunnah which are not performed in any place except in Madinah.” Imam (a.s) said: “They are performed in the Mosque of the Messenger (saws), peace be upon him and his family, on Eid, before one goes out to the place of prayer. This is not (done) except in Madinah, because the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, did it.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« رَكْعَتَانِ مِنَ اَلسُّنَّةِ لَيْسَ يُصَلَّيَانِ فِي مَوْضِعٍ إِلاَّ بِالْمَدِينَةِ» قَالَ «يُصَلَّى فِي مَسْجِدِ اَلرَّسُولِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فِي اَلْعِيدِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ إِلَى اَلْمُصَلَّى لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ بِالْمَدِينَةِ لِأَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَعَلَهُ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Eat on the day of al-Fitr, before you go out to the place of prayer.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اِطْعَمْ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ إِلَى اَلْمُصَلَّى»

items.e: And from him, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Jarrah al-Mada’ini, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Eat on the day of al-Fitr before you pray, and do not eat on the day of al-Adha, until the Imam has finished and departed.”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ جَرَّاحٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« اِطْعَمْ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ وَ لاَ تَطْعَمْ يَوْمَ اَلْأَضْحَى حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفَ اَلْإِمَامُ»

items.e: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Said al-Naqqash, who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: “Indeed, there is Takbir (proclamation of 'Allahu Akbar') in al-Fitr, but it is Sunnah (recommended).” He (al-Naqqash) said: “I asked, ‘And when is it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “On the night of al-Fitr, in (the prayers of) Maghrib and the final Isha, and in the prayer of Fajr and the prayer of Eid, then it is discontinued.” He (al-Naqqash) said: “I asked, ‘How should I say it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “You say: ‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illa Allah (swt), wa-Allahu Akbar wa lillahi al-hamd, Allahu Akbar ala ma hadana’, And this is the saying of Allah (swt): ‘So that you may complete the prescribed period and glorify Allah (swt) for guiding you’. (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185)”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِاَ للَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ خَلَفِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ سَعِيدٍ اَلنَّقَّاشِ قَالَ: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لِي« أَمَا إِنَّ فِي اَلْفِطْرِ تَكْبِيراً وَ لَكِنَّهُ مَسْنُونٌ» قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ أَيْنَ هُوَ قَالَ« فِي لَيْلَةِ اَلْفِطْرِ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ وَ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدِ ثُمَّ يُقْطَعُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ أَقُولُ قَالَ تَقُولُ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَ لِلَّهِ اَلْحَمْدُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ عَلَى مَا هَدَانَا وَ هُوَ قَوْلُ اَللَّهِ« وَ لِتُكْمِلُوا اَلْعِدَّةَ وَ لِتُكَبِّرُوا اَللّٰهَ عَلىٰ مٰا هَدٰاكُمْ»

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “And remember Allah (swt) during the appointed days” (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:203). Imam (a.s) said: “The Takbir (proclamation of 'Allahu Akbar') is during the Days of Tashriq, from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer on the third day. And in the cities, it is for ten prayers. So when one departs (from Mina) after the first (departure), the people of the cities stop. And whoever remains in Mina and performs the Dhuhr and Asr prayers there, then let him proclaim the Takbir.”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ« وَاُذْكُرُوا اَللّٰهَ فِي أَيّٰامٍ مَعْدُودٰاتٍ» قَالَ« اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي أَيَّامِ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ صَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ مِنْ يَوْمِ اَلنَّحْرِ إِلَى صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ يَوْمَ اَلثَّالِثِ وَ فِي اَلْأَمْصَارِ عَشْرَ صَلَوَاتٍُ فَإِذَا نَفَرَ بَعْدَ اَلْأُولَى أَمْسَكَ أَهْلُ اَلْأَمْصَارِ وَ مَنْ أَقَامَ بِمِنًى فَصَلَّى بِهَا اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ فَلْيُكَبِّرْ»

items.e: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, said: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the Takbir during the Days of Tashriq after the prayers. Imam (a.s) said: “The Takbir in Mina is after fifteen prayers, and in the other cities (amsar), it is after ten prayers. The first of the Takbir is after the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr). You say in it; ‘Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest for what He has guided us to, Allah (swt) is the Greatest for what He has provided us from the beast of cattle.’ And the reason the Takbir was made for ten prayers in the other cities (amsar), is that when the people depart in the first departure (al-nafr al-awwal), the people of the cities cease from the Takbir, while the people of Mina continue to proclaim the Takbir as long as they remain in Mina, until the final departure (al-nafr al-akhir).”
items.o: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي أَيَّامِ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ فِي دُبُرِ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ فَقَالَ« اَلتَّكْبِيرُ بِمِنًى فِي دُبُرِ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ صَلاَةً وَ فِي سَائِرِ اَلْأَمْصَارِ فِي دُبُرِ عَشْرِ صَلَوَاتٍُ أَوَّلُ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي دُبُرِ صَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ يَوْمَ اَلنَّحْرِ تَقُولُ فِيهِ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَاَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ عَلَى مَا هَدَانَا اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ عَلَى مَا رَزَقَنَا مِنْ بَهِيمَةِ اَلْأَنْعَامِ وَ إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ فِي سَائِرِ اَلْأَمْصَارِ فِي دُبُرِ عَشْرِ صَلَوَاتٍُ اَلتَّكْبِيرُ أَنَّهُ إِذَا نَفَرَ اَلنَّاسُ فِي اَلنَّفْرِ اَلْأَوَّلِ أَمْسَكَ أَهْلُ اَلْأَمْصَارِ عَنِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ وَ كَبَّرَ أَهْلُ مِنًى مَا دَامُوا بِمِنًى إِلَى اَلنَّفْرِ اَلْأَخِيرِ»

items.e: Ali ibn Hatim from Sulayman al-Zurari from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sadan ibn Muslim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Abi Mansur from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “You say between every two Takbirs in the Eid prayers: ‘O’ Allah (swt), Possessor of Majesty and Greatness, Possessor of Generosity and Might, Possessor of Forgiveness and Mercy, Possessor of God-consciousness and forgiveness. I ask You (azj) on this day which You (azj) have made a festival for the Muslims and a treasure and increase for (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that You (azj) send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), with the best of what You (azj) have sent upon any servant from among Your servants, and that You (azj) send blessings upon Your nearest angels and Your messengers, and that You forgive the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women, those among them who are living and those who are deceased. O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) for the best of what Your sent servants have asked You (azj) for, and I seek refuge in You (azj) from the evil of that from which Your sent servants sought refuge.’”
items.o: عَلِيُّ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ اَلزُّرَارِيِّ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ أَبِي مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« تَقُولُ بَيْنَ كُلِّ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ اَللَّهُمَّ أَهْلَ اَلْكِبْرِيَاءِ وَ اَلْعَظَمَةِ وَ أَهْلَ اَلْجُودِ وَ اَلْجَبَرُوتِ وَ أَهْلَ اَلْعَفْوِ وَ اَلرَّحْمَةِ وَ أَهْلَ اَلتَّقْوَى وَ اَلْمَغْفِرَةِ أَسْأَلُكَ فِي هَذَا اَلْيَوْمِ اَلَّذِي جَعَلْتَهُ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ عِيداً وَ لِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ذُخْراً وَ مَزِيداً أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَأَفْضَلِ مَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى عَبْدٍ مِنْ عِبَادِكَ وَ صَلِّ عَلَى مَلاَئِكَتِكَ اَلْمُقَرَّبِينَ وَ رُسُلِكَ وَ اِغْفِرْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ اَلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ اَلْمُسْلِمَاتِ اَلْأَحْيَاءِ مِنْهُمْ وَ اَلْأَمْوَاتِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ مَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادُكَ اَلْمُرْسَلُونَ وَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا عَاذَ بِكَ مِنْهُ عِبَادُكَ اَلْمُرْسَلُونَ»

items.e: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abi Jamilah from Jabir from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “When the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, used to pronounce the Takbir during the two Eids, He (a.s) would say between every two Takbirs; ‘I bear witness that there is no God but Allah (swt), alone, without partner, and I bear witness that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) is His (azj) servant and His (azj) messenger, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. O’ Allah (swt), Possessor of Majesty’” And Imam (a.s) mentioned the supplication to its end, as previously stated.
items.o: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا كَبَّرَ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ بَيْنَ كُلِّ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ اَللَّهُمَّ أَهْلَ اَلْكِبْرِيَاءِ»» وَ ذَكَرَ اَلدُّعَاءَ إِلَى آخِرِهِ مِثْلَهُ

items.e: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn Atiyyah from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Supplicate on the two Eids and on the day of Jumu’ah, when you have prepared yourself to go out, with this supplication: “O’ Allah (swt), whoever has made preparations, and mobilized himself, and prepared and readied himself for an arrival before a created being, hoping for his gifts, seeking his bounty, his rewards, his generosity, and his surplus offerings then my arrival, O’ my Master, is to You (azj); And my preparation, and my readiness, and my equipping, and my preparation again, are for You (azj), hoping for Your gifts, Your rewards, and Your generous offerings. So do not disappoint my hope today, O’ You (azj) in Whom no supplicant is ever disappointed, and Whose bestowal is never diminished, I have not come to You (azj) today with a righteous deed that I have sent forward, nor with the intercession of a created being, in whom I placed hope. Rather, I have come to You (azj) acknowledging my wrongdoing and misdeeds. I have no proof and no excuse. So I ask You (azj), O’ my Lord (azj), to grant me my request, to return me with what I seek, and not to turn me back disappointed or deprived. O’ Great One! O’ Great One! O’ Great One! I beseech You (azj) by the Great, I ask You (azj), O’ Great One, to forgive me the great (sins). There is no God, but You (azj). O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and grant me the good of this day which You (azj) have honored and magnified. Cleanse me on it from all my sins and misdeeds, and increase me from Your bounty. ‘Indeed, You are the Bestower’. (Surah Sa’ad 38:35)”
items.o: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ اَلثُّمَالِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اُدْعُ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ وَ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ إِذَا تَهَيَّأْتَ لِلْخُرُوجِ بِهَذَا اَلدُّعَاءِ اَللَّهُمَّ مَنْ تَهَيَّأَ وَ تَعَبَّأَ وَأَعَدَّ وَاِسْتَعَدَّ لِوِفَادَةٍ إِلَى مَخْلُوقٍ رَجَاءَ رِفْدِهِ وَطَلَبَ نَائِلِهِ وَجَوَائِزِهِ وَفَوَاضِلِهِ وَنَوَافِلِهِ فَإِلَيْكَ يَا سَيِّدِي وِفَادَتِي وَ تَهْيِئَتِي وَ تَعْبِئَتِي وَ إِعْدَادِي وَ اِسْتِعْدَادِي رَجَاءَ رِفْدِكَ وَ جَوَائِزِكَ وَ نَوَافِلِكَ فَلاَ تُخَيِّبِ اَلْيَوْمَ رَجَائِي يَا مَنْ لاَ يَخِيبُ عَلَيْهِ سَائِلٌ وَ لاَ يَنْقُصُهُ نَائِلٌ فَإِنِّي لَمْ آتِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ بِعَمَلٍ صَالِحٍ قَدَّمْتُهُ وَ لاَ شَفَاعَةِ مَخْلُوقٍ رَجَوْتُهُ وَ لَكِنْ أَتَيْتُكَ مُقِرّاً بِالظُّلْمِ وَ اَلْإِسَاءَةِ لاَ حُجَّةَ لِي وَ لاَ عُذْرَ فَأَسْأَلُكَ يَا رَبِّ أَنْ تُعْطِيَنِي مَسْأَلَتِي وَ تَقْلِبَنِي بِرَغْبَتِي وَ لاَ تَرُدَّنِي مَجْبُوهاً وَ لاَ خَائِباً يَا عَظِيمُ يَا عَظِيمُ يَا عَظِيمُ أَرْجُوكَ لِلْعَظِيمِ أَسْأَلُكَ يَا عَظِيمُ أَنْ تَغْفِرَ لِيَ اَلْعَظِيمَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَاُرْزُقْنِي خَيْرَ هَذَا اَلْيَوْمِ اَلَّذِي شَرَّفْتَهُ وَعَظَّمْتَهُ وَ تَغْسِلَنِي فِيهِ مِنْ جَمِيعِ ذُنُوبِي وَ خَطَايَايَ وَ زِدْنِي مِنْ فَضْلِكَ« إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَلْوَهّٰابُ»

items.e: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hamadhani narrated to us; he said: Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti narrated to us; he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Abdi narrated to us; he said: I heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Fasting on the day of Ghadir Khumm, equals the fasting of the lifetime of the world, if a person were to live and fast for as long as the world lasts, the reward of that would be for him. And its fasting equals, in the sight of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, in every year, one hundred accepted Hajj and one hundred accepted Umrah. And it is the greatest Eid of Allah (swt), and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has never sent any prophet except that he celebrated Eid on this day, recognized its sanctity, and knew its name. In the heavens it is called the ‘Day of the Promised Covenant’, and on the earth it is the ‘Day of the Taken Pledge’ and the ‘Witnessed Gathering’. Whoever prays two rak‘ahs on this day having performed ghusl (ritual bathing) at the time of the sun's zenith, half an hour before it begins to decline and supplicates to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and in each rak‘ah recites Surah al-Hamd (once), and ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) ten times, and Ayat al-Kursi (ten times), and ‘Inna anzalnahu’ (ten times); it would equal, in the sight of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, one hundred thousand Hajj and one hundred thousand Umrah. And he would not ask Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for any need from among the needs of this world or the Hereafter, except that it would be fulfilled whatever that need may be. And if you missed the two rak’ahs and the supplication, you may perform them later. And whoever gives iftar (breaks the fast) of a believer on this day, it would be as if he had fed an army, and an army, and an army (and Imam (a.s) kept counting until he reached ten with his hand).” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Do you know how many are in an army (fiam)?” I said: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “One hundred thousand. Each army would carry the reward of one who fed the same number from among the Prophets, the Truthful, and the Martyrs in the Sacred Sanctuary of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and gave them drink ‘on a day of severe hunger’. And a dirham (spent) on this day is equal to a million dirhams.” Imam (a.s) said: “Perhaps you think that Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has created a day more sacred than this? No, by Allah (swt)! No, by Allah (swt)! No, by Allah (swt)!” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And let it be from your words when you meet one another that you say: ‘All praise is due to Allah (swt), who honoured us with this day and made us among those who fulfill His (azj) covenant with us, and His (azj) pledge which He (azj) bound us to concerning the guardianship of the leaders of His (azj) command and the ones who uphold His (azj) justice and did not make us among the deniers and rejecters of the Day of Judgement.’” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And let it be from your supplication after these two rak’ahs that you say: ‘Our Lord (azj), indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, saying: ‘Believe in your Lord (azj),’ so we believed. Our Lord (azj), forgive us our sins, and expiate from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous. Our Lord (azj), and grant us what You (azj) promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You (azj) do not break the promise.’” (Imam (a.s) then continued) “Then you say after that; ‘O’ Allah (swt), I call You (azj) to witness and You (azj) are sufficient as a witness and I call to witness Your angels, the bearers of Your Throne, the inhabitants of Your heavens and Your earth, that indeed You (azj) are Allah (swt), there is no God but You (azj), the One to be worshipped. There is no being from beneath Your Throne to the depths of Your earth, that is rightfully worshipped besides You (azj); anything else that is worshipped is false and perishing, apart from Your Noble Face. There is no God but You (azj), the One to be worshipped; so none is worthy of worship besides You (azj). Exalted are You (azj) above what the wrongdoers say, with great exaltation. And I bear witness that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, is Your servant and Your Messenger (saws).
